blocks.text: Condo buildings in East Cambie
Streets, schools and transit near East Cambie condos

items.t: East Cambie is in the City of Richmond, on the east side of the city, abutting the Agricultural Land Reserve along No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway; it is an official City planning area (the East Cambie Area Plan, Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan). The Area Plan's boundary maps are graphics whose roads are not stated in the plan text.

Main roads named in the plan: Cambie Road, No. 5 Road and Westminster Highway, with Highway 91 (the Richmond Freeway) and the Alex Fraser Bridge (named "Annacis Bridge" in the plan text) giving the area its cross-river access. West Cambie is to the west, Bridgeport to the north-west, and ALR farmland runs along the No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway edges.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere, in apartment form. The documented base form is single detached housing; the Area Plan anticipated residential projects along some major roads at townhouse or apartment densities, and the built strata product that has actually been verified in this area is townhouse form on and near the Cambie Road / No. 5 Road corridors.

The commercial node is the south-west corner of Cambie Road and No. 5 Road — the Area Plan names it the principal community commercial area (Cambie Plaza), with the Richmond Auto Mall as an existing smaller commercial centre; Richmond Public Library's Cambie Branch is at 150-11590 Cambie Road in that node and Cambie Community Centre is at 12800 Cambie Road.

Transit: the one timetable service confirmed pass is the TransLink 430 Express stopping on Garden City Road at Cambie Road at the area's west edge, running between Richmond-Brighouse Station and Metrotown Station.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in East Cambie

items.t: Richmond zoning and plans: the area's base zone is Single Detached (RS1/RS2) under Zoning Bylaw No. 8500 — the RS1/E subzone documented on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550.0 m², minimum width 18.0 m and minimum depth 24.0 m, with one principal dwelling per lot and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. The East Cambie Area Plan is Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan (adopted October 21, 2002; Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874) under the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000; the City began a further OCP update process in fall 2024 toward a 2050 horizon. In East Cambie, multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the Area Plan.

Suites / SSMUH: the City states it allows at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot on covered lots, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots.

Flood rules — the Richmond-specific diligence item: all lands within Richmond are designated flood plain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204, which sets flood construction levels (FCLs) that habitable floors must meet unless an exemption applies; Richmond sits at an average of 1 metre above sea level behind 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 flood event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way, and the Area Plan requires new development in East Cambie to provide adequate flood protection. Strata insurance and FCL compliance are building-specific checks on any East Cambie strata purchase.

Richmond money dates: 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid taxes after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% penalty on any outstanding balance after Tuesday, September 1, 2026; annual flat-rate utility payments were due March 31, 2026, with a 10% discount only for payments received on or before the due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Cambie condos

items.t: The plan is older than the townhouses. The East Cambie Area Plan was adopted October 21, 2002 (Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874) and already anticipated corridor townhouse/apartment densities — Cambie Gardens (2005) and Wembley (2020) are that 2002 plan arriving, a generation apart. The City also began a further OCP update in fall 2024 toward a 2050 horizon, so the plan framework over any new strata here is mid-revision.

The area's biggest park is a bog inside the ALR. Richmond Nature Park, 11851 Westminster Highway, is 100+ acres of old bog forest with the Nature House interpretive centre, the Area Plan conserves it as a bog environment, and the plan also protects Bath Slough as a natural watercourse — the "green edge" beside the townhouse corridors is protected bog, not future development land.

Mitchell Elementary carries a heritage ask. The Area Plan asks the School Board to conserve the Mitchell School buildings as heritage structures, and Mitchell is the longest continuously operating school in the Richmond public system, named after Richmond pioneer Alex Mitchell — relevant context for any redevelopment expectation near the Cambie / No. 5 node.

King George / Cambie Community Park is the plan's anchor park. At 4100 No. 5 Road, with heritage trees, courts, playgrounds, tennis and a waterpark, the Area Plan calls it the principal community park, to be retained and expanded on its present site — the amenity the Thorpe Road and No. 5 Road townhouse stock actually lives beside.

The bridge in the plan has two names. The Area Plan text calls the Alex Fraser Bridge the "Annacis Bridge" — older planning documents, listing copy and local speech for this area use both names for the same Highway 91 crossing that gives East Cambie its Delta and Surrey access.

items.t: Form B diligence (all 8 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a 13-unit complex like Cambie Gardens, the Form B is effectively the whole financial picture. Listing-level rental/pet lines here are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

Richmond zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw 8500 governs — the area's base zone is Single Detached (RS1/RS2) under Section 8.1, and the RS1/E subzone documented on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550.0 m², minimum width 18.0 m and minimum depth 24.0 m, with one principal dwelling per lot and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. Townhouse sites proceed under low-density townhouse zones (the RTL4 rezoning record in is the worked example) and multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the Area Plan. The East Cambie Area Plan is Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan (adopted October 21, 2002; Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874) under the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000.

Flood — the Richmond-specific diligence item: all lands within Richmond are designated flood plain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204, which sets flood construction levels (FCLs) that habitable floors must meet unless an exemption applies; Richmond sits at an average of 1 metre above sea level behind 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 flood event, with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way, and the Area Plan requires new development in East Cambie to provide adequate flood protection. Strata insurance and FCL compliance are building-specific checks on any East Cambie strata purchase.

blocks.text: Lots and land in East Cambie
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established-street house lots: single detached housing is the documented base form.

Lot character from the zone: the RS1/E subzone documented on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550.0 m², minimum width 18.0 m and minimum depth 24.0 m under Zoning Bylaw 8500, Section 8.1 (RS1/RS2), with one principal dwelling per lot and a secondary suite as a permitted secondary use. These are zone figures for that subzone, not a claim about any existing lot's size; other subzones apply elsewhere in the area and are confirmed with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR split, as the plan states it: the East Cambie Planning Area abuts the Agricultural Land Reserve along No. 6 Road and Westminster Highway, the Richmond Nature Park is within the ALR, and a plan goal is a distinct boundary between agricultural and non-agricultural lands. The ALR ground is therefore at the area's east and Westminster Highway edges, not interleaved through the residential streets on this evidence.

Flood position — citywide, no exceptions on this evidence: Richmond is made up of islands within the floodplain of the Fraser River at an average of 1 metre above sea level, behind a flood protection system of 49 km of dikes designed for a 1:500 event (0.2% chance in any year), with dike raising from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres under way; all lands within Richmond are designated flood plain under Bylaw No. 8204, and the Area Plan says new development in East Cambie is to provide adequate flood protection.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in East Cambie

items.t: Plan: the East Cambie Area Plan is Schedule 2.11B to the Official Community Plan (plan adoption October 21, 2002; Land Use Map updated by Bylaw 9874), under the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000 (Schedule 1); the City began a further OCP update process in fall 2024 toward a 2050 horizon.

SSMUH / suites as the City states them: the City states it allows at least one secondary suite and/or accessory dwelling unit per lot on covered lots, with Bill 44 small-scale multi-unit minimums of 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on larger lots.

ALR rules (the area genuinely abuts ALR ground, so these bite at the edges): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Heritage note for lot diligence near the node: the Area Plan asks the School Board to conserve the Mitchell School buildings as heritage structures, and Mitchell Elementary is the longest continuously operating school in the Richmond public system — relevant context for redevelopment expectations near the Cambie Road / No. 5 Road node, not a lot rule.

The bridge in the plan has two names: the Area Plan text calls the Alex Fraser Bridge the "Annacis Bridge" — older planning documents, listing copy and local speech for this area use both names for the same Highway 91 crossing that gives East Cambie its Delta and Surrey access.

faq.a: The strata product that exists here is townhouse form (Cambie Gardens, Wembley, the Thorpe Road complex).
faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in East Cambie?

faq.a: The Area Plan anticipates townhouse or apartment densities along some major roads, multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the plan, and a City application already documents an RS1/E-to-RTL4 townhouse rezoning at 11671/11691 Cambie Road — the direction is corridor strata, townhouse first.
faq.q: Will apartment condos ever be built here?

faq.a: Yes, structurally: all of Richmond is designated flood plain under Bylaw No. 8204 with flood construction levels for habitable floors, and strata insurance pricing in Richmond reflects the dike-and-floodplain setting (49 km of dikes, 1:500 design event, dike raising to 4.7 m under way). Ask for the building's FCL compliance and insurance terms rather than assuming from the map.
faq.q: Does flood risk affect a strata purchase here?

faq.a: Schools physically in the area: Mitchell Elementary (3800 No. 5 Road), Kathleen McNeely Elementary (12440 Woodhead Road) and H.J. Cambie Secondary (4151 Jacombs Road); SD38 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12). King George Secondary is a Vancouver (SD39) school and has no bearing here, despite a past filing error.
faq.q: Which schools serve an East Cambie townhouse?

faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. A short-term rental bylaw can still bind you, and the specific complex's registered bylaws are read in the strata package.
faq.q: Can I rent out an East Cambie townhouse?

faq.a: Townhouses: eight known strata complexes — Cambie Gardens (11331 Cambie Road, 13 duplex-style townhomes, built 2005), Wembley (4991 No. 5 Road, by Citimark, built 2020, 109 townhomes per the presale record), Normandie (11571 Thorpe Road, 77 units), Cambie Court (12311 Cambie Road), and the Polygon-era McNeely / Jack Bell pocket: Sausalito, Francisco Village, Capistrano and Malibu.
